hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $\overline{BF}$

Under this transformation, some points on the quadrilateral map to another point which is no longer on the quadrilateral.  


[[☃ image 1]]

The quadrilateral is *not symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: A quadrilateral A C D E where sides A E and A C are congruent and sides D E and D C are congruent. Angles E and C are congruent acute angles. Side A E has a midpoint F. Side A C has a midpoint B. A blue line connects from midpoints F and B, reflecting the quadrilateral. The image of the reflected quadrilateral has vertices A C and E outside of the pre-image.

hints.content:
##Reflection over $\overline{AD}$

Under this transformation, each point on the quadrilateral maps to another point which is also on the quadrilateral.


[[☃ image 1]]

The quadrilateral is *symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: A quadrilateral A C D E where sides A E and A C are congruent and sides D E and D C are congruent. Angles E and C are congruent acute angles. Side A E has a midpoint F. Side A C has a midpoint B. A blue line connects from vertices A and D, reflecting the quadrilateral. The image of the reflected quadrilateral is completely on the pre-image.

hints.content:
The symmetries that apply to the quadrilateral are:

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{BF}$ | No
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{AD}$ | Yes
